examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Distance Given Speed and Time
examples.problem: Moving at a constant rate, it takes $8$ seconds for a particular type of fish to swim a distance of $200$ centimeters. Find the distance this fish can cover in $3$ seconds.
examples.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in centimeters per second, we divide the number of centimeters, $200,$ by the number of seconds, $8.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{200}{8} & =200÷8 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the fish is $25$ centimeters per second. 

To find the distance covered in $3$ seconds, we multiply the speed by $3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{distance} & =\text{speed}\times \text{time} \\  & =25\times 3 \\  & =75.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fish can cover $75$ centimeters in $3$ seconds.

feedback.problem: A starfish moves $12$ miles in $20$ hours, moving at a constant pace. What is the speed of the starfish?
feedback.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed (in miles per hour), we divide the number of miles, $12,$ by the number of hours, $20.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{20} & =\frac{12÷2}{20÷2} \\  & =\frac{6}{10} \\  & =6÷10 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of starfish is $0.6$ miles per hour.
